result.description: Fires mainly on the "une" piece in "fine-tune" (also "fine tuning"), where something is being adjusted or regulated. It stays silent on "une" in "immune". Weaker hits on other word pieces.
result.label: "tune" in fine-tune

result.description: Fires on function words (mostly "the", "an", "a") in text about black holes and event horizons, where the next word is likely a black-hole term such as Hawking, Event, or Schwarzschild. Silent on "the" in other cosmology contexts.
result.label: Determiners before black-hole terms

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ities' completing "externalities" (also 'b' in "herb"), in economics text on externalities and public goods. It stays quiet on 'ities' in other words like "irregularities".
result.label: "external-ities" suffix token

result.description: Fires on a plural abstract noun (ideas, problems, designs, themes, equations) right after "complex", "intricate" or "complicated". It stays silent on "themes" without such a preceding adjective. Logits favour continuations like "involving", "requiring" and "simpler".
result.label: Noun after complex/intricate adjective

result.description: Fires on prepositions (mostly ' of', also in/from/by) right after "collective behavior" in swarm intelligence text, predicting a following plural noun like "decentralized" agents. Silent on 'of' after other nouns such as design, aim, help.
result.label: 'of' after "collective behavior" (swarm)

result.description: Fires on the final word or piece of an academic topic or field name (Conflict, relationships, dynamics, integration, equilibrium, language) in heading-like lists. It pushes toward 'theories', 'systems', 'theory'. Peaks are mixed and consistency is low.
result.label: Academic topic-term endings in headings

result.description: Fires on the word "there" (or "There") as the existential subject starting a clause, e.g. "there is/are/may be", at sentence start or after a conjunction or colon. Members are mostly "there" detectors.
result.label: Existential "there" clause subject

result.description: Fires on adjectives or comparative modifiers (different, simple, complex, -er, ordinary, remaining) in cooking and culinary text, where a noun like ingredients, cuts or flavors is expected next. Silent on non-modifier tokens in the same cooking passages.
result.label: Culinary adjective/modifier before food noun

result.description: Fires on 'and', commas, 'or' that join items in a list of verb phrases (actions or practices) where a new verb in -ing/base form comes next. Silent on 'and' joining plain nouns in a list.
result.label: Conjunction before next verb phrase

result.description: Fires on word-ending pieces like 'ic', 'mic', 'ple', 'th' in technical chemistry/thermodynamics words (exothermic, endothermic, participle, affinity). Silent on 'ic' in other words like symbolic or isochoric. Members are chemistry-reaction context.
result.label: Chemistry word suffix pieces (exothermic)

result.description: Fires on particles and verb-completing tokens after a verb, such as "coming out", "comes together", "pops up" and "sprouted". It also fires weakly on a stray digit. Silent when " out" is inside a word like "outlet" or in "sniff out". The evidence is mixed.
result.label: Verb particles: out, together, up

result.description: Fires on connecting function words and verb endings (such as, by, includes, -ates) in biology/psychology/stress passages, where a biological or cognitive term is expected next. Silent on "such as" in cooking and genre text.
result.label: Connectives in biology/stress text

result.description: Fires on the word " virtue" (also "principle", virtue-word pieces) in moral philosophy and virtue-ethics text. Members are mostly virtue detectors plus philosophy-context members. Predicts suffixes like "-hood" or "-ality".
result.label: virtue in ethics discussion
' virt' word-piece before 'ues/uous'
result.description: Fires mainly on the word piece ' virt' (start of virtues/virtuous), with weaker hits on ' product', ' where' and similar prefixes. It predicts suffixes like 'uous' and 'ues'. Members are mostly ' virt' detectors.

Fires mostly on the word piece " mel" (as in melody) in music-related text, with weaker peaks on " and" in lists and on "op" in Mesopotamia. It predicts word continuations like "ody". The circuit is mixed and only partly faithful.
result.label: " mel" start of melody

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' lear' when it begins "learner" (a lear|ner), in education text. It is silent on the full word "learning". Members include other word-start fragment detectors that predict the 'ner' continuation.
result.label: ' lear' as start of learner

result.description: Fires on the word piece " pen" (also " Pen"), usually as the start of a longer word such as penetration, penalty or peninsula, and also in the standalone noun "pen". It predicts continuations like "etr", "alt" and "chant".
result.label: " pen" word-start token

result.description: Fires on the word-start piece ' ster' (also ' Ster') when it begins a longer word like steroid or sterile. Members are detectors of other word-initial fragments (fert-, cot-, ris-, invas-) that predict a continuation.
result.label: ' ster' word-start fragment

result.description: Fires on ' Dr' at the start of a new line in a list of names (e.g. "Dr. Johnson.¶ Dr. Williams."). Stays silent on lists of names without the Dr title. Weak activity on a few list commas.
result.label: ' Dr' in name lists

result.description: Fires on capitalized acronym pieces like 'ER' and 'NER' (also POS, NL) in technical text, such as Entity-Relationship (ERD) or Named Entity Recognition (NER) in NLP/ML contexts. Predicts acronym continuations like NER or POS.
result.label: NLP/database acronym 'ER'/'NER'

result.description: Fires on varied words (those, together, over time, student, and) in text about people collaborating, connecting and sharing ideas. Logits favour ' themselves', ' they', ' independently', ' alone'. Peaks are inconsistent, and the evidence is mixed.
result.label: Collaboration and togetherness text, mixed tokens

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' proc' at the start of "procurement" (or "procure"), mostly in supply chain text. Members detect ' proc' and similar word-start pieces like ' rec', ' alloc' and ' fil'.
result.label: ' proc' in procurement

result.description: Fires on varied function words and verbs (allows, of, in, enabling, developing) in technical or academic text about technology and research, where a plural noun like methods, tools or ways is likely next. Mixed peaks, low consistency; evidence is thin.
result.label: Technical text slot before plural nouns

result.description: Fires on art/discipline nouns like "writing", "fiction", "painting" when a modifier precedes and the term is the subject of a comparison (e.g. "formal writing", "informal writing"). It predicts verbs like "excel", "tends", "typically". Silent on some "writing" uses.
result.label: Genre/discipline noun as subject

result.description: Fires on the verb (mostly ' is', also ' can', ' be') right after an abstract subject like mastery of or understanding a skill or concept, where an evaluative predicate such as essential, crucial or necessary comes next. Silent when there is no such subject.
result.label: Verb after skill/understanding subject

result.description: Fires mostly on the word piece 'iv' inside multi-piece words like capt-iv-ating, p-iv-otal, omn-iv-ores, predicting a suffix such as 'ating' or 'otal'. Weaker on some other mid-word pieces (mult, tri, fasc-in).
result.label: 'iv' mid-word piece (captivating)

result.description: Fires on incomplete word-start fragments, mostly ' multip' (before "licity") and 'omed' in "Biomedical", where the next piece completes the word. Members are mostly ' multip' detectors plus other word-start pieces such as retr, quant, cul and emp.
result.label: Word-start fragments: multip, omed

result.description: Fires on "that", "to", "which" or a comma after a noun or verb in text about symbols, maps and visual communication. It sits where a verb like convey, communicate or denote is expected next. It stays silent on "that" in other topics.
result.label: Symbol-conveying relative 'that'/'to'

result.description: Fires on connector words and commas (such as, including, like, of) in water-cycle and hydrology text where a list of components or factors is about to follow. Predicts water/model/simulation terms. Silent on plain 'of' elsewhere.
result.label: Hydrology list-introducing connectors

result.description: Fires on ' of' directly after "one" (also "some") in the partitive "one of the most/many…" construction. It stays silent on ' of' after nouns like "terms", "part", "challenge", "demands".
result.label: 'of' in "one of the"

result.description: Fires on the word piece "or" inside "rhet-or-ic" (rhetor, rhetorical, rhetorician), predicting suffixes like -ic, -ical, -ician. Also weakly on similar mid-word pieces such as "aud-it". Silent on "or" in other words like "elect-or-ate".
result.label: "or" inside rhetor-ic words

result.description: Fires on the token ' ten' (as number, in "nearest ten", "power of ten", or as the start of "tenor"). It is silent on unrelated text. Logits favor suffix pieces like 'or', 'acity', 'ets', so it seems to treat ' ten' as a word-start piece.
result.label: ' ten' token detector

result.description: Fires mainly on commas inside a list of items, especially the SMART goals acronym list (Specific, Measurable, Achievable). Silent on commas in ordinary prose clauses, such as "for example," or "on the other hand,".
result.label: Commas in SMART-style lists

result.description: Fires on plural subject nouns like "databases" (also "systems", "which", "that") when they are the subject of a clause about NoSQL or non-relational databases, just before a verb like "are designed to". It stays quiet when "databases" is an object or follows a preposition.
result.label: NoSQL databases as clause subject

result.description: Fires on the suffix 'ing' (or 'ating') ending an evaluative adjective like intrigu-ing or fascin-ating, before a noun such as puzzle, aspect or prospect. Silent on verb -ing endings like deconstructing or analyzing.
result.label: Adjective -ing in intriguing/fascinating

result.description: Fires on the token ' hands' (occasionally ' hand'), most strongly in 'hands-on' phrases about learning, and also in hand-washing text. It pushes the next token towards '-'. It stays silent on 'manual'.
result.label: ' hands' token, as in hands-on

result.description: Fires weakly and inconsistently on varied mid-phrase tokens (' of', ' in', ' new', ' previous', word pieces like ' Sem', 'ing') in academic or encyclopedic text. No clear shared token or construction; the logits are mixed.
result.label: Diffuse mid-phrase academic tokens

result.description: Fires on commas, "for", "of" and verbs within lists or noun phrases of technical processes (planning, production, design, engineering) in technical expository text; silent on other commas. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Technical process list separators

result.description: Fires on 'by', 'that', 'within' or 'of' right after "goods and services (produced)" in economics definitions of aggregate supply or output. It predicts a producer-type noun next (producers, firms). It stays silent on 'that' as a complementizer or relative pronoun elsewhere.
result.label: Economics 'goods and services produced by'

result.description: Fires on ' highlight' (also ' eng', ' Lock') as a finite verb after a subject noun, as in "design highlighted the importance" or "philosophy highlights". It stays silent on the infinitive "serves to highlight".
result.label: Verb 'highlight' after a subject

result.description: Fires on ' of' right after a technical math noun like derivative, kernel, rank, or null space, where a mathematical object follows ("kernel of a matrix"). It stays silent on ' of' after words like aspect, collection, or use.
result.label: ' of' after math object nouns

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' fer' that starts "fermentation" (mid-sentence, in biology/food-science text), predicting the continuation "ment". Silent on ' fer' at the start of "fermenting" in the contrast. Weak activity on a few other word fragments.
result.label: ' fer' in fermentation

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (' were', ' the', ' of', ' closely', word endings like 'lings') where the next word is likely a verb or continuation in academic prose. Peaks are inconsistent; the evidence is mixed and the pattern is diffuse.
result.label: Diffuse mid-clause academic continuation

result.description: Fires on varied mid-sentence words (verbs, adjectives, determiners like "the", "your", "unique", "significant") in explanatory academic-style text, where a noun is expected next. Peaks are scattered and inconsistent; logits are weak and the circuit is diffuse.
result.label: Diffuse mid-phrase word before noun

result.description: Fires on mid-word fragments of science words that are incomplete and need a continuation, such as 'ilib' in Equilibrium, 'ov' in photovoltaic, and ' energ' in energies. It fires in technical or scientific text, on the word piece before the suffix.
result.label: Incomplete science word fragments (ilib, ov, energ)

result.description: Fires on "distribution" or "density" (also "spread") in probability/statistics text, where the next word is likely "function" (as in cumulative distribution function, probability density function). Needs a probability-theory context.
result.label: Probability distribution/density before "function"

result.description: Fires on connecting function words (as, and, use, include, from, in) that introduce a list or example in text about animal behavior, predators and species. Silent on "such as" in other subject areas like disease or research.
result.label: Connectives before lists in animal-behavior text

result.description: Fires on a bare space token that precedes digits (e.g. a year or number after "between", "the late") and on the piece ' pred' in "predator/predation" after prepositions. Silent on some spaces before numbers after "under"/"during the".
result.label: Space before number / ' pred' piece

result.description: Fires on the word " lives" (plural of life), mostly after a possessive or article such as "our lives" or "the lives of". Members are detectors of lives/life tokens in earlier layers. Weakly fires on " life" and " people".
result.label: " lives" after possessive/article

result.description: Fires on varied tokens (control, focus, and, in) in passages about attention and cognitive control, e.g. "attention control" or "better focus". Silent on "control" in engineering or interpersonal contexts. Evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Attention/cognitive control passages

result.description: Fires on abstract nouns like "world", "space", "relationships", "reality" ending a phrase in geometry/spatial-reasoning text (e.g. "three-dimensional world", "understanding of space"). Silent on some "relationships" tokens in the same topic.
result.label: Spatial-concept nouns in geometry text

result.description: Fires at the end of "Development Goals" (als/s) and the following " (" where an acronym like MDG/SDG is about to be given. Silent on ordinary words ending in "als" such as "professionals".
result.label: Development Goals before acronym

result.description: Fires on "important", "crucial" (cru-cial) and "essential" in the predicate of an "'s important/crucial to…" clause that follows a sentence end. Silent on "crucial" in some other contexts, such as "…ity is crucial for".
result.label: important/crucial after "'s" clause

result.description: Fires on " to" or " and" right after a starting year in a date range ("from 1750 to", "between 1900 and"), where the end year is expected next. Silent on " to" in other uses.
result.label: Year range connector before end year

result.description: Fires on 'and' or commas right after visual-art element nouns like shape, form, line in lists of art elements (e.g. "shapes and lines"), predicting another element or property like function, size, space. Silent after 'depth and'.
result.label: Art elements list: shape/form and

result.description: Fires on the 'rich' piece in the verb or noun 'enrich' (enrichment, enriching, enriched), where a suffix like -ment or -ed is expected next. Members are 'rich' detectors plus similar stem pieces such as 'emp-ower' and 'augment'.
result.label: 'rich' inside 'enrich-' words

result.description: Fires on the suffix piece "itive" completing "cognitive" (also "neurological", "neural") in neuroscience or psychology text, where a noun like processes, systems or development comes next. Quiet on "repetitive" and some other "cognitive" contexts.
result.label: "cognitive" suffix in neuroscience text

result.description: Fires on " of" (also in/to/for) right after a noun like "aspect", "part", "component" in "became an important/integral/essential aspect of X". Silent on other " of" uses such as "dawn of" or "explosion of".
result.label: "became integral part of" preposition

result.description: Fires on quantifier-like adjectives (various, different, multiple, diverse) right after verbs or prepositions of combining/integrating (combine, integration of, balancing), before a plural noun like types, sources, layers. Silent after "in/across various domains".
result.label: various/different after combining verbs

result.description: Fires on the final token of an abstract noun naming the inner nature of something, mostly "ence" in "essence", also " structure", " nature", " properties", where "of X" typically follows. Silent on "ence" in other words like prevalence or interdependence.
result.label: essence/nature noun before "of"

result.description: Peaks are scattered across unrelated tokens (word pieces, ' of', spaces, ' models') in abstract academic or essay-style prose. Consistency is low and the contrast shows no clear rule. The circuit is diffuse and its members are mostly generic context.
result.label: Diffuse academic-prose mid-phrase tokens

result.description: Fires on function words (for, on, the, comma, are) in text about bacterial conjugation and horizontal gene transfer, where the next word is likely pili, conjugative or transfer. Silent on 'the' in general genetics text.
result.label: Function words in bacterial conjugation text

result.description: Fires on mixed word pieces such as 'ent' in "attentiveness", 'uts' in "nuts", 'iry' and commas, mostly mid-word fragments in expository lists. It is silent on 'ent' in "inherent" and "attentive", so the evidence is thin and mixed.
result.label: Mid-word fragments in lists (ent, uts)

result.description: Fires on mixed tokens, most often the 'i' in "Idioms" at document start, plus hyphens, ' can', ' of' and ' services'. Peaks are scattered with low consistency. It seems to predict a word-continuation piece, but the evidence is thin.
result.label: Scattered peaks, 'i' in Idioms

result.description: Fires on the word " down" as a directional word, especially in up/down pairs (quarks, movement) and before "ward"/"stream"/"hill". Pushes toward suffixes like "ward", "stream" and "grade". Silent in the currency "value" contrast text.
result.label: ' down' directional word

result.description: Fires on " can" right after a subject noun like "origins", "roots" or "origin of X", where the next words are likely "be traced" or "be linked". Silent on " can" after other subjects, such as "compositions can provide".
result.label: "can" after origins/roots subject

result.description: Fires on function words and commas (the, a, of, ",") right after a geological era or epoch description (Cenozoic, Holocene) where the next word would be a geologic period or event name, e.g. "marked the", "Era,". Silent on commas in other text.
result.label: Function words in geologic epoch text

result.description: Fires on mid-word pieces 'unction' (as in conjunction) and ' val' (valence, valves, valued), where the word continues with a suffix such as -s, -al or -ence. Mostly conjunction-related text; members detect 'unction'.
result.label: 'unction' / 'val' word-piece

result.description: Fires on a gerund (' providing', '-ing' pieces like introducing, enlarging, engaging) right after "by", i.e. a "by + V-ing" means clause. Silent on ' providing' after a comma or "also". Predicts an object pronoun like them/it/their.
result.label: gerund after "by" (by V-ing)

result.description: Fires on abstract plural or noun endings (practices, states, theories, diversity, perspectives) that finish a coordinated list of social or cultural concepts, e.g. "gender roles and practices". Silent on some "practices" in other lists. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: Social-concept noun after "and"

result.description: Fires on scattered tokens, most often the 'igen' piece in lowercase "indigenous", plus ' engineering', ' mapping', ' the' in academic text. It is silent on 'igen' in capitalized "Indigenous". Evidence is mixed and the peaks are inconsistent.
result.label: Scattered peaks, 'igen' in indigenous

result.description: Fires on ' are' (or ' is') right after a plural subject noun inside a clause introduced by "ensure/guarantee that", e.g. "ensure that all controls are". Predicts adverbs or state words like properly, correctly, not. Silent in plain descriptive statements.
result.label: are/is after "ensure that" subject

result.description: Fires on the word piece 'ith' inside words like lithium, lithography, monolith and lithosphere, where it follows 'l' or 'ol'. Silent on other text. Members are mostly 'ith' detectors in earlier layers.
result.label: 'ith' piece in lithium/lithography

result.description: Fires on the adjective " rich" (also "lush"), as in "richness", "rich and varied", "rich, loamy soil", "rich and poor". It predicts suffix continuations like -ness, -est and -er. Silent on text without it.
result.label: ' rich' adjective token

result.description: Fires on varied word pieces and tokens (mostly 'ing' in "lighting", 'le', ' Species', '-') with low consistency. Logits favor ' light', ' day', ' natural'. Evidence is mixed and the circuit failed faithfulness.
result.label: Mixed word pieces, lighting-like

result.description: Fires weakly and inconsistently on varied function words (' of', ' in', ' and', ' appear', quotes) mid-phrase in abstract expository prose. It is silent on many ' of' cases, and the evidence for what separates them is unclear.
result.label: Scattered function words in expository prose

result.description: Fires on function words (be, to, that, plural -es) in definitional text about countable/uncountable nouns and grammar, predicting count-related words like 'count', 'counted', 'finite'. Silent on ' be' in other contexts.
result.label: Countable-noun definition function words

result.description: Fires on the word " throughout" when it follows a noun phrase and introduces a span such as "the narrative", "history" or "all stages". Pushes the next token toward "the", "all", "each" and "history".
result.label: ' throughout' after a noun phrase

result.description: Diffuse target peaking on mixed tokens (' and', ' possibly', 'imal', ' for', word fragments) in academic, expository prose. Silent on many ' and' contexts, and the evidence does not show what separates them. Members are weak and generic.
result.label: Scattered tokens in academic prose

result.description: Fires on function words (mostly " of") after a verb or noun in international law, treaty, or environmental regulation text (use of, protection of), predicting legal or international objects like nuclear, illegal, rights. Silent on " of" in general social text.
result.label: " of" in treaty/regulation text

result.description: Fires on the word-piece " inter" when it is a prefix to be completed, as in government inter|vention, inter|ference, inter|play. It predicts continuations like "vention", "vent", "ference".
result.label: inter- prefix mid-word

result.description: Fires on the word piece " ideal" (also "Ide-al", "Orth" at heading starts) when it is a stem likely continued by a suffix such as -ism, -ized, -ization. Predicts those suffixes next. Mostly in philosophy and idealism text.
result.label: ' ideal' stem before suffix

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and mid-phrase tokens (of, in, the, own, state) inside abstract expository text about systems, societies, or biology, where a noun like "system" may come next. No dominant token; the evidence is mixed and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Function words in abstract expository text

result.description: Fires on ' in' following a research/work/occurrence noun or verb in academic science text (e.g. "research in", "work in", "occurred in"), introducing a field or time. Silent on ' in' after "increase", "resulted", or "transformation".
result.label: ' in' after research/work nouns

result.description: Diffuse target peaking on varied tokens (' initial', ' change', ' as', '/') mostly in economics or academic explanatory text, such as the multiplier effect. Peak tokens are inconsistent and members are weak, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Diffuse economics-explanation tokens

result.description: Fires on the noun naming a person's intellectual output (theory, work, model, experiment, problem) right after a famous thinker's possessive name, e.g. "Plato's theory", "Rutherford's later work". Silent on "work" without a possessive thinker.
result.label: Thinker's possessive, then their work

result.description: Fires on frequency adjectives/adverbs like "regularly", "regular", "routine", "frequent" before maintenance-type actions (inspections, cleaning, checks, updates). Predicts words like scheduled, updates, checks.
result.label: Regular/routine maintenance frequency words

result.description: Fires on scattered function-word or suffix tokens (' in' after "lies", 'ic' in "volcanic", ' by', ' its', possessive S) in abstract expository prose, where the next word is likely an abstract noun like success or recognition. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is weak.
result.label: Scattered function words in expository prose

result.description: Fires on the word piece "astronom" (astronomy, astronomers) and on "ua" in "lingua franca". Two separate token detectors with mixed support; the contrast text shows no clear extra condition.
result.label: astronom- and lingua franca

result.description: Fires on social media platform names (Twitter, the 'agram' of Instagram) inside lists after phrases like "social media platforms like Facebook, ...". Supported by members detecting Twitter, Instagram and "social media".
result.label: Social media platform names in lists

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' pron' at the start of "pronoun" or "pronunciation", predicting continuations like 'oun', 'unci', 'ounced'. Weakly fires on 'on' in "Pronunciation". Silent on "pronominators" after 'proct'.
result.label: ' pron' word-start piece

result.description: Fires on medical/drug/surgical modifier words (' drug', ' medical', 'ical', 'ive') in materials-science text listing biomedical applications, predicting application nouns like implants, devices, delivery, prostheses.
result.label: Medical modifier before device nouns

result.description: Fires on scattered function words (to, of, on, in, more) and word pieces like "du", mostly after likelihood/contribution words (likely to, probability of, contribute to). Peaks are mixed and the circuit is weak; members are generic.
result.label: Scattered function words after likelihood

result.description: Fires on modifier words (certain, written, official, personal) right after "in/inside/of" that precede a noun like works, documents or settings. It predicts a noun naming a kind of text or publication. Peaks are scattered and weak.
result.label: Adjective after "in" before text noun

result.description: Diffuse target peaking on varied mid-word pieces and function words (ive, into, and, to, speaking, include) in expository text; no consistent token or context. Silent on 'ive' in adjectives like inclusive. Members are generic.
result.label: Diffuse mixed-token expository latent

result.description: Fires on the piece 'ot' inside words like "homotopy" (also phenotype, totipotent, Vygotsky), where the next piece is likely 'opy' or 'ype'. It stays silent on 'ot' in "knot".
result.label: 'ot' inside hom-ot-opy words

result.description: Fires on forms of "foster" (fost-ers, fost-er, encourag-es) and the following connecting words (" of", " for", " and") in text about fostering collaboration, creativity or engagement. It predicts nouns like belonging, team, connections. It is silent on agent-noun "-ers" such as listeners.
result.label: fostering verb endings, collaboration-themed

result.description: Fires on word-start pieces like ' established', ' legit', ' eleg', ' synchron' that are likely to be continued or modified into a longer word (legitimizing, elegance). Fires only moderately and inconsistently; silent on some ' established' uses.
result.label: Word-start pieces: established, legit, eleg

result.description: Fires mostly on " for" (also "ools", "irregular", "itional") in linguistics/grammar text, especially after terms like inflectional or derivational markers ("the derivational n-y symbol for adverbs"). Silent on ordinary " for" in other phrases. Evidence is mixed.
result.label: ' for' after grammatical affix terms

result.description: Fires on the token ' reporting' (as a noun/gerund, e.g. "automated reporting", "reporting standards"). Upstream members are mostly ' reporting' detectors across layers. Weakly fires on ' reports'. Pushes towards ' on'.
result.label: ' reporting' token detector

result.description: Fires on mid-clause adverbs like " also", " only", " both" sitting between a plural or subject noun and its upcoming verb, where a verb like support, contribute or aim comes next. It is silent on some " also" cases.
result.label: Adverb before verb (also)

result.description: Fires on ' new' (also ' novel', ' fresh') right after creation or development verbs (create, creation of, development of, generate, open up), predicting category nouns like types, kinds or ways. Silent after adopt, incorporate, open to.
result.label: 'new' after creation verbs

result.description: Fires on the prefix ' meta' (as in meta-analysis, meta-narrative) and on 'format' inside 'bioinformatics', where a scientific or technical word continues. Predicts suffix pieces like 'ometric' and 'ose'.
result.label: meta- / bioinformatics word prefix

result.description: Fires on the mid-word fragment 'rig' in "irrigation" (also 'per' in "repertoire/repercussions", 'el' in "indelible"), a word piece inside a longer word that is still being completed. Predicts word-completing suffix pieces like 'toire'.
result.label: 'rig' in irrigation word-piece

result.description: Fires on the 'ing' piece in "lasting" (last+ing), as in "lasting impression/impact". It stays silent on 'ing' in other words like bonding, enriching or thriving. It pushes towards nouns like impact, impression and effects.
result.label: 'ing' in "lasting"

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' ir' when it begins "irony" (and related ironic forms) in literary or rhetorical text. It predicts continuations like "ony". It is silent on the whole word "ire".
result.label: ' ir' starting "irony"

result.description: Fires on pieces of person names (first names, surnames, name fragments like "ily", "Jess", " Johnson") inside lists of names, one per line, e.g. "Dr. Smith.¶ Dr. Emily Johnson.¶". Also fires weakly on scattered other tokens. Peaks are mixed.
result.label: Names in line-separated lists

result.description: Fires on the word-piece ' sequ' (start of "sequencing", "sequential") and predicts continuations like "encing", "ential", "enced". Weakly fires on other incomplete word starts such as ' tren' and ' mach'.
result.label: ' sequ' word-start piece
Change-of-state verbs before adverb/continuation
result.description: Fires on verbs or particles describing change, escalation or increase/decrease (blurred, flare up, builds up, more serious, negotiation) in abstract essay-like text. Members detect rise/fall/increase verbs. The next token is likely an adverb or continuation like "among" or "significantly".

Fires on the verb or relative word right after a plural noun like "methodologies", "approaches" or "techniques" in "this section explores…" text (" used", " employed", " that", " taken"). It predicts a passive "used/employed" continuation. It is silent on "that" after security strategies.
result.label: Methods noun followed by used/employed

result.description: Fires on the word piece ' rational' (rational numbers, rationalism, rationality, rational agents) and predicts suffix continuations like 'ity', 'ism', 'thinking'. Members are mostly ' rational' detectors across layers. The contrast text lacks the token.
result.label: ' rational' token detector

result.description: Fires mainly on the degree sign '°' in temperature or coordinate expressions, especially the second one in a pair like 165°F (74°C), where a unit letter follows. Occasional weak firing on ' opt' and some function words.
result.label: Degree sign before unit letter

result.description: Fires on modal verbs ' can' (also ' may', ' could') directly after the relative pronoun "which" (or "this") that continues a clause, as in "..., which can then be...". Silent on 'can' after plain nouns or "one".
result.label: Modal 'can' after "which"

result.description: Fires on the last token of a process noun (evolution, change, dispersal, diversification, diversity) after a subject like species or language, in academic text on biology or linguistics. It predicts words like dynamics, path, trajectories and patterns.
result.label: Species/language change process nouns

result.description: Fires on ' considered' after a passive "is/are/be" when something is described as regarded in a certain way (e.g. "is considered a masterpiece"). Weaker on near-synonyms like "viewed". Predicts evaluative continuations such as "one", "the", "to".
result.label: passive "is considered" (regarded as)

result.description: Fires on ' of' directly after the noun "aspect(s)" (e.g. "a fundamental aspect of"), predicting a gerund or topic next. Silent on ' of' after other nouns like "implementation", "standards", "understanding".
result.label: ' of' after "aspect"

result.description: Fires on function words (the, a, for, this, behind) in creative/artistic writing, where the next word is likely an abstract noun like "success" or "triumph". Members detect create/artist/story contexts. Silent on many "the" tokens, so the condition is unclear.
result.label: Function words in creative-writing contexts

result.description: Fires on words right after "withstand/resist/endure" (e.g. "harsh", "relentless", "the", "moisture") where a threat or harsh condition comes next. Predicts nouns like attack, assault, damage, shock. Silent on "the" after generic verbs like "address" or "deal with".
result.label: Withstanding harsh conditions or attacks

result.description: Fires on the possessive 's after a person's name (e.g. "Richard Garwin's"), where the next word is likely about their work, contributions, legacy or philosophy. Silent on 's after common nouns or pronouns like "one's" or "project's".
result.label: Possessive 's after person names

result.description: Fires on goal-directed words like " towards", " toward", " achieve" and "ieving", mostly in leadership or teamwork text about guiding people to goals. It predicts goal-like nouns next (goals, shared, common, object).
result.label: towards / achieve before goals

result.description: Fires on ' level'/' levels' right after 'sea' in earth-science text (sea level rise, regulation). Stays silent on 'levels' after other nouns like salt, carbon dioxide or elevation. Weaker on other measure nouns (temperature, type).
result.label: 'sea level' in earth science

result.description: Fires on prepositions (to, between, with, in) right after passive participles like "subjected" or "sandwiched" in physics/semiconductor text. It stays silent on "to" after "lead", "related" or "corresponding".
result.label: Preposition after subjected/sandwiched (physics)

result.description: Fires on ' the' directly after a verb like predict, study, capture, or account for in technical science/math prose, where an abstract noun like behavior, effects, or properties comes next. It is silent on ' the' after prepositions or in other positions.
result.label: 'the' after science analysis verbs

result.description: Fires on the word ' in' when it directly follows a coordinating 'and' or 'or' (e.g. "and in return", "and in person"), starting a parallel phrase. Silent on ' in' after verbs or nouns like "role in" or "aid in".
result.label: ' in' after 'and'/'or'

result.description: Fires on scattered function words and punctuation (' to', ' the', ',', ')', ' in') in abstract expository prose; stays silent on many ' to' tokens in other uses. Peaks are inconsistent and the circuit is weak, so the pattern is unclear.
result.label: Scattered function words in expository text

result.description: Fires on mixed tokens in expository science/technology text: word-piece 'och' in mitochondria, function words like ' to' or ' the', and mid-word pieces. Likely predicts a technical noun continuation. Evidence is diffuse and the circuit failed.
result.label: Mixed word pieces in technical text
